summary: Round 2 review of a71922bf. The fixes for all four round-1 findings work, and the latest code introduces no regression. PRR-01: validate_result now requires the full observed_contract object. It must equal request['contract'] key by key, and the controller computes its digest itself, so an echoed hash no longer passes. All four evidence files must be distinct absolute paths inside the sample folder; resolved symlink escapes are rejected. PRR-02: the executed source is kept as .executed.py.txt with a warning to copy it to external scratch before running it. selected-status-doc.json is committed and matches the audit: document _id, run 49 to end, uint64 (3,32,512,1024), 50331648 elements times 8 bytes = 402653184 bytes. audit-provenance.json is honestly labelled as a post-audit readback. PRR-03: every true qualification flag now adds its receipt to the required artifacts, and each missing receipt is tested. Two flags reuse ordinary input artifacts as their receipts (event_reference, calibration_manifest); the instructions say so. PRR-04: the timeout test reads the child's real PID and checks the process is gone after termination. A relative adapter_command[0] is rejected. Everything else from round 1 still holds: the freeze, identity, phase and allocation gates, the balanced AB/BA schedule, A/A with the baseline on both sides, the T95 indexing and outcome labels, the all-false default qualification flags, and the run51 Confluence distinction from mfx100852324 runs 77-79. The docs keep the pixel_status audit separate from full calibration and durable dataset qualification, and claim no native execution, hardware result or dataset permanence. On the boundary: the deliverable is still a controller plus an adapter contract, not a template that runs end to end. That matches the agreed scope and is stated plainly, but no PR can be measured until someone writes and reviews a revision-specific adapter. There is one new non-blocking low-severity finding (PRR-05).

findings.evidence: When a sample is accepted, execute writes exit.json (returncode, wall_seconds) but records no hash of result.json. The evidence hashes are supplied inside result.json itself. summarize (line 301-304) re-reads result.json and the evidence files and only checks that they agree with each other. So a coordinated edit after acceptance (for example changing loop_seconds in result.json) passes summarize undetected. regression/README.md:47-48 and pr-regression.md:171 say results remain immutable, but the controller does not enforce this.
findings.requested_change: After validate_result succeeds in execute, record the SHA256 of result.json and of each evidence file, in exit.json or a per-sample accepted.json. Have summarize require these to match. Add a test that edits loop_seconds after execute and expects summarize to reject it.
